correctness.rationale: The frozen proof at RESULT.md line 50 had an incorrect nonzero covariance prefactor. Write p=q² and J=(p;p)_∞. The published theta omits the factor J, while the frozen displayed theta includes it. Translating Eq. (2.30) to that convention requires J³/θ(−r;p), not J²/θ(−r;p). Independently, as u→1 from below, (1−u) times the defining Laurent sum tends to 1 (the positive-tail coefficient differs from 1 by a summable correction, and the negative tail stays bounded); θ(u;p)/(1−u)→J³, also forcing the corrected factor. A separately written 65-digit check at p=.09,r=.5,u=.4 gave a series–product residual below 10⁻⁶³ with the corrected prefactor, versus about −0.19858 as printed. Complete corrected RESULTS and self-review files are in /workspace/repairs/2/ (RESULT.md and REVIEW.md); the Finding is unchanged. In the repaired proof, the numerator zeros are exactly −ru=p^k with boundary products excluded; for nonintegral ξ the only admissible k is ceil ξ. Proper Gaussianity makes covariance zero equivalent to independence. Lift to the log strip, map it by exp(iπ(w+L)/L) to the upper half-plane, and minimize over deck lifts; the cosh formula increases in the magnitude of the lifted angular displacement, giving ±π for these product pairs. At fixed mean angle θ0=π{ξ}, letting b=sin²t measure radial imbalance gives cosh d=1+(cosh(π²/L)−1+2b)/(sin²θ0−b), strictly increasing on the admissible domain. Thus b=0 is the unique radial configuration, giving the orbit and exact arsinh distance. The core length is 2π²/L by the strip metric on its central geodesic, yielding the sharp half-length bound; at exceptional weights there is no pair, and sin(π{ξ})=sin(πh/(2L)) gives the stated divergence constant. Replay: repaired RESULT.md lines 41–83; arXiv:2008.04177v3 Eqs. (2.10)–(2.12), (2.30), Lemma 2.3. The supplied checker was inspected, not executed and does not test the normalization identity; the finite independent check only corroborates the analytical correction.
